nodes.label: Agent Pre-processing System
nodes.rationale: The analysis agent itself can be attacked by hostile content in the malware sample, so a pre-processing system must rule-detect and map agent inputs before the agent runs its analysis workflow.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Evidence & Mapping
nodes.rationale: Detection must yield evidence of the attack plus a mapping to MITRE ATLAS / OWASP LLM Top 10 so the finding is actionable; when no trace is found the analysis agent is allowed to continue.

nodes.label: Detection Rule & Agent Input Mapping
nodes.rationale: Rules must be defined over the exact data types the agent consumes, so that each MITRE ATLAS / OWASP LLM Top 10 attack class maps to a pre-processing decision.

nodes.label: Neurosymbolic Defense-in-Depth Guardrail
nodes.rationale: No static rule set can block 100% of adversarial prompts in an unbounded natural-language space (NIST/Vassilev incompleteness proof); deterministic filters must therefore be combined with semantic ML guardrails, prompt isolation and runtime execution rails.

nodes.label: Threat Model for Promptware Against Analysis Agent
False Positive Dilemma
nodes.rationale: Ordinary malware always contains system-command strings (cmd.exe /c powershell -enc, bypass, admin, eval()); a guardrail must separate legitimate malware behaviour strings from Agent-manipulation commands without flagging the former.

nodes.label: Normalization & De-obfuscation Engine
nodes.rationale: Obfuscated payloads (Base64, Hex, Leetspeak, homoglyphs, zero-width characters) defeat plain keyword/regex filters, so decoding and Unicode normalization must run before YARA and the ML classifier.

nodes.label: Decision Policy Matrix
nodes.rationale: Three graded responses are offered because reaction must stay proportional to investigation context: Tag-as-Evidence preserves analysis value, Sanitize/Drop removes the payload, Hard Block stops the pipeline for system-threatening injections.

nodes.label: Tag-as-Evidence Policy
nodes.rationale: Recommended default: do not destroy the malware analysis; neutralize the injected command by turning it into passive data and tagging it as Anti-Agent / Evasion behaviour (T1497 / AML.T0051) in the final report.

nodes.label: Sanitize / Drop Policy
nodes.rationale: When a payload cannot be safely retained as evidence it is replaced with a safe placeholder such as [REDACTED_PROMPT_INJECTION] before reaching the Agent.

nodes.label: Hard Block Policy
nodes.rationale: Reserved for injections that threaten the analysis system itself, where continuing the pipeline is unacceptable.

nodes.label: Runtime Execution Rails & Output Governance
nodes.rationale: Even if the Agent's reasoning is hijacked, least-privilege execution rails must deny shell, file-write and network-egress tools so no harmful action is reachable.

nodes.label: Microsoft Azure AI Prompt Shields & Spotlighting
Layer 0 - Normalization & De-obfuscation Engine
nodes.rationale: Bounded recursive decoding (max depth 2, 64 KB block, ASCII printable ratio >= 80%) is limited on purpose to avoid mis-decoding shellcode binaries while still peeling common encoding layers.

nodes.label: Layer 2A - CAPA Data Abstraction
nodes.rationale: The Agent is most exposed when reading free-text raw strings and disassembly; CAPA converts them into structured ATT&CK capability JSON, eliminating ~95% of the promptware attack surface while retaining 100% of behavioural value.

nodes.label: Layer 4 - Decision Policy Gate & Prompt Isolation
nodes.rationale: Tag-as-Evidence is chosen over dropping the sample so adversarial instructions become passive evidence rather than lost intelligence; strict XML delimiters keep the instruction channel separate from the untrusted malware data channel.

nodes.label: Layer 5 - Runtime Execution Rails & Output Governance
nodes.rationale: Least privilege is enforced by never registering shell, file-write or network tools, so a manipulated Agent has no capability to cause harm, and JSON-Schema validation constrains its output.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Read-Only Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Only three query functions (get_pe_header_details, get_mitre_capabilities, get_quarantined_evidence) are exposed; capability removal, not prompt wording, is the last line of defence.

nodes.label: Spotlighting XML Delimiters
nodes.rationale: Untrusted telemetry is wrapped in system_policy, untrusted_malware_telemetry and quarantined_adversarial_evidence tags so the model can tell data from instructions, and any command inside them is defined to be an evasion attempt.
